candidates.statement: Comments and suggestions regarding this draft document should be submitted within 60 days of publication in the Federal Register of the notice announcing the availability of the draft guidance. Submit electronic comments to http://www.regulations.gov . Submit written comments to the Division of Dockets Management (HFA-305), Food and Drug Administration,
candidates.context: Updating ANDA Labeling After the Marketing Application for the Reference Listed Drug Has Been Withdrawn Guidance for Industry DRAFT GUIDANCE This guidance document is being distributed for comment purposes only.

candidates.statement: This guidance describes a process for updating labeling for abbreviated new drug applications 17 (ANDAs) in cases where FDA has withdrawn approval of the new drug application (NDA) 2 for 18 the ANDA’s reference listed drug (RLD) 3 for reasons other than safety or effectiveness. Where 19 approval of the NDA for the RLD has been withdrawn by FDA under these circumstances 20 (referred to in this guidance as a “withdrawn RLD”), and ANDAs are pending or generic drugs 21 continue to be marketed under one or more ANDAs that rely on the withdrawn RLD, the 22 labeling of those pending or marketed ANDA products may need to be updated to reflect 23 changes that would have been necessary had the NDA for the RLD not been withdrawn. 24
candidates.context: This guidance sets forth ways in which FDA may seek to facilitate the revision of labeling to 26 reflect updated information for ANDAs that rely on withdrawn RLDs. This guidance will be of 27 interest to the holders of pending or approved ANDAs that rely upon a withdrawn RLD, as well 28 as to applicants seeking to submit ANDAs relying on withdrawn RLDs. We anticipate that this 29 guidance will help facilitate labeling updates for approved ANDAs as well as the approval of 30 certain pending ANDAs where the NDA for the RLD has been withdrawn. 31

candidates.statement: A generic drug is required to have the same labeling as the RLD at the time of approval, except 42 for changes required because of differences approved under a suitability petition (see section 43 505(j)(2)(C) of the FD&C Act and 21 CFR 314.93) or because the generic drug and the RLD are 44 “produced or distributed by different manufacturers” (see section 505(j)(2)(A)(v) of the FD&C 45 Act). FDA regulations provide examples of permissible differences in labeling that may result 46 where a proposed generic drug and the RLD are “produced or distributed by different 47 manufacturers,” including the omission of an indication or other aspect of labeling protected by 48 patent or exclusivity and “labeling revisions made to comply with current FDA labeling 49 guidelines or other guidance.” 21 CFR 314.94(a)(8)(iv). 50
candidates.context: As a general matter, all holders of marketing applications for drug products (both NDAs and 52 ANDAs) have an ongoing obligation to ensure their product labeling is accurate, and not false or 53 misleading. When new information becomes available that causes the labeling to become 54 inaccurate, false or misleading, the application holder must take steps to update its labeling (see, 55 e.g., 21 CFR 201.56(a)(2)). Any drug is misbranded if its labeling is false or misleading, or does 56 not provide adequate directions for use and adequate warnings (sections 301(a) and (b), and 57 502(a), (f), and (j) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) (21 U.S.C. 331(a) 58 and (b), and 352(a), (f), and (j))). 59

candidates.statement: Where an RLD has been withdrawn, ANDA products that were approved in reliance on the 81 withdrawn RLD may continue to be marketed, and new ANDAs must refer to the withdrawn 82 RLD as the basis for ANDA submission (provided that there has been a determination that the 83 NDA RLD was not withdrawn for reasons of safety or effectiveness) (see § 314.122(c) (21 CFR 84 314.122(c))). 85
candidates.context: (21 CFR 314.150(c))). 4 As noted above, withdrawal of an NDA RLD under these circumstances 78 is referred to in this guidance as a “withdrawn RLD.” 5 Under these circumstances, where approval of the NDA for an RLD has been withdrawn, the 87 NDA holder can no longer update labeling for the withdrawn RLD. 6 Yet as a drug is used over 88 time, the scientific community’s understanding of the drug may evolve based on data from 89 various sources, including published literature and postmarketing data. Therefore, the labeling 90 of ANDAs that rely on the withdrawn RLD might eventually become inaccurate and outdated, 91 resulting in labeling that is false and/or misleading, for example. Likewise, new original 92 ANDAs that rely on the withdrawn RLD might include proposed labeling based on the last 93 approved RLD labeling that includes outdated information that is false and/or misleading. 94

candidates.statement: If an NDA for a certain drug has been withdrawn, there may be other drugs that contain the same 96 active ingredient (or an active ingredient in the same pharmacologic or therapeutic class) for 97 which approval of the NDA has not been withdrawn. The labeling of those other drugs, as well 98 as the labeling of any corresponding ANDAs, may have been updated to reflect any new 99 scientific information that is needed for the safe and effective use of the drug. This creates a 100 situation in which certain NDAs and ANDAs for a given active ingredient have up-to-date 101 labeling, while other ANDAs do not, simply because those other ANDAs rely on an RLD for 102 which approval of the NDA has been withdrawn. In such cases the labeling of pending ANDAs 103 or marketed ANDAs products may need to be updated to reflect changes that would have been 104 necessary had the NDA for the RLD not been withdrawn. 105

candidates.statement: 6 In cases where marketing of the RLD product has been discontinued but approval of the NDA has not been withdrawn under § 314.150 or section 505(e) of the FD&C Act (referred to in this guidance as a “discontinued RLD”), the NDA holder must still comply with applicable statutory and regulatory requirements. These requirements include, for example, proposing any necessary revisions to update product labeling for the discontinued RLD (see, e.g., § 201.56(a)(2)). ANDA products approved in reliance on a discontinued RLD may continue to be marketed, and new ANDAs must refer to the discontinued RLD as the basis for ANDA submission (see § 314.122(c)). The Agency will continue to list discontinued RLD drug products on the “Discontinued Drug Product List” in FDA’s “Approved Drug Products With Therapeutic Equivalence Evaluations” (the “Orange Book”), unless FDA determines that the drug product was withdrawn from sale for reasons of safety or effectiveness, in which case the drug product will be removed from the Orange Book.

In this guidance, FDA clarifies that consistent with the statute, where the RLD is withdrawn, 107 certain labeling changes may continue to be made for pending ANDAs and marketed ANDAs. 7

candidates.statement: ANDA holders are responsible for reviewing postmarketing data and published literature as 131 appropriate to satisfy applicable reporting requirements (e.g., 21 CFR 314.81, 314.98). 132 However, FDA (as well as ANDA holders and applicants) may be aware of data relevant to 133 labeling updates in a variety of situations. For example, relevant data may already be reflected in 134 the updated labeling of other drugs in the same pharmacologic or therapeutic class (e.g., class 135 labeling); in non-product specific literature; or in postmarketing information. The updates 136 contemplated by this guidance generally would not involve reliance on product-specific, 137 proprietary information about another drug. Any changes proposed under this guidance must be 138 consistent with the requirement that an ANDA include sufficient information to show that the 139 conditions of use have been previously approved for the RLD (section 505(j)(2)(A)(i)). 140
candidates.context: IV. UPDATING LABELING OF ANDAs THAT RELY ON WITHDRAWN RLDs 129 7 The approach proposed in this guidance is consistent with FDA statements made in the context of determinations that certain drug products that have been withdrawn from sale were not withdrawn for reasons of safety or effectiveness, including statements to the effect that “[i]f FDA determines that labeling for these drug products should be revised to meet current standards, the Agency will advise ANDA applicants to submit such labeling.” See, e.g ., 80 FR 27320 at 27321 (May 13, 2015) (determining that SODIUM SULAMYD (sulfacetamide sodium) Ophthalmic Solution and Ophthalmic Ointment were not withdrawn from sale for reasons of safety or effectiveness).

candidates.statement: The FDAAA SLC process is separate and distinct from the process described in this guidance. 263 FDA will continue to use its FDAAA SLC authorities where appropriate in situations where 264 FDA becomes aware of “new safety information” about a serious risk or an unexpected serious 265 risk that the Agency believes should be included in product labeling. 266 This guidance addresses certain situations in which needed updates to the labeling of ANDAs 267 that rely on withdrawn RLDs may not be captured by the FDAAA SLC process. For example: 268 • The FDAAA SLC authorities apply only to approved NDAs and ANDAs. When new 269 original ANDAs are submitted that rely on a withdrawn RLD, the FDAAA SLC 270 authorities do not extend to the draft labeling submitted as part of those pending 271 applications. Under this guidance, FDA will consider the FDAAA SLC notification that 272 is sent to the holders of approved applications to be “FDA labeling guidelines or other 273 guidance” within the meaning of § 314.94(a)(8)(iv). Applicants with pending ANDAs 274 will be able to submit amendments to their applications with labeling that reflects the 275 safety labeling change made by the holders of approved ANDAs relying on the same 276 RLD, and this will be considered a change made to comply with “current FDA labeling 277 guidelines or other guidance” within the meaning of the regulation. 278
